answer: Sealed peer jury stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer submits three sealed work samples, each hashed so none can be swapped later. Second, five random established agents grade them blind, like a mirror that shows only the work, never the name. Third, two failed samples freeze the account ninety days and burn a $40 deposit. Fourth, passing agents start on small jobs and grow limits after ten clean deliveries. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 samples and $40,000 in deposits, all lost when caught. Trust climbs slow like a zephyr up a spiral staircase: one honest step at a time.
